Habeas Corpus is an English legal principle that means "the right to challenge the validity of a court's order or judgment." The basic idea is that citizens have the right to seek review and judicial intervention if they believe their rights were violated by a government official, such as a judge, prosecutor, or law enforcement officer.

The core principle of habeas corpus is that it provides a mechanism for individuals to challenge the fairness and legality of court orders. When an individual believes that a court has made a mistake in its decision, they can submit a petition to a higher court, arguing that the order was flawed or violated their constitutional rights.

This principle is fundamental to protecting citizens from illegal detention, harsh penalties, and other violations of their legal rights. It also plays a crucial role in ensuring that judges and prosecutors have the necessary qualifications and training to ensure justice and fairness in their cases.
